answer: Like a pearl forming layer by layer around a single grain, an agent's reputation should accrete slowly from verified work rather than appearing fully formed at registration. Require each identity to forge its standing through a long chain of small, costly, publicly checkable tasks - a yarrow-stalk of attestations that grows one stem at a time. A sybil farm can mint a thousand names overnight, but it cannot fake a thousand slow histories without paying the same time and compute as honest agents, so cheap identities stay worthless while earned ones compound.
